meeting_header: Date: 2026-07-01 | Time: 09:00-09:45 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Ari (Redwood AE), Jess (Redwood SE), Marcus (Redwood CSM), Mark (Novus Eng Lead), Priya (Novus Sec/Infra), Elena (Novus PM), Samir (Novus SRE), Liam (Novus DS)
summary: Weekly POC check-in. Reviewed onboarding progress: VPC peering pending, service account and KMS access outstanding. Shared initial perf numbers from Redwood Dedicated trial; discussed tuning for latency vs cost and quantization tradeoffs. Security questions around audit logs and key management flagged; Redwood to send SOC2/ISO artifacts. Agreed next steps to exchange network details and schedule a live benchmark next week.
topics: Access setup: VPC peering, service accounts, KMS
Environment readiness: test dataset, GPU instance choices
Results review: early perf numbers, latency/cost tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Ari (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining on time, we'll keep this tight, agenda is onboarding status, access, and a quick results review.
[00:18] Mark: thanks Ari, yep we're keen to get the live perf test scheduled. we tried the sample calls last week, saw some higher p99s than expected.
[00:33] Jess (SE): got it. quick context: the numbers you saw were from the default config on Redwood Dedicated with 16k context and no quantization, so some room to tune. can you remind us which payloads you used?
[00:49] Liam (Data Scientist): mostly the chat prompts from our support assistant, average length ~380 tokens, but a subset with long docs to summarize. we sent a sample csv to the dropbox link.
[01:05] Jess: cool, thanks. that helps — long docs will hit KV cash warmup and affect p99. we usually test with prefix caching enabled.
[01:20] Priya (Sec): quick interrupt — from our side we still don't have the service account or KMS access configured. we raised an internal ticket but need a checklist.
[01:33] Ari: understood. action item: we'll share our security checklist and SOC2 artifacts after the call. Jess, can you include the KMS hookup steps?
[01:42] Jess: yes, I'll include the steps for both customer-managed KMS and Redwood-hosted options, notes on key rotation and HSM integration.
[01:55] Mark: on the VPC peering front, Samir's been blocked by CIDR collision concerns with our existing overlays.
[02:05] Samir (SRE): yep, our infra team flagged that the dev VPC ranges overlap with Redwood's default. we need to confirm peerable ranges or use private link.
[02:16] Ari: ok we can do private-link as a fallback. Priya, do you prefer private-link or peering?
[02:24] Priya: prefer peering for latency but private-link is acceptable if peering isn't possible due to CIDR. we'll send our VPC diagram after the call.
[02:35] Elena (PM): timeline check — we want performance results before the exec review on 2026-07-20. is that doable?
[02:45] Jess: yes, if we get VPC access and the sample dataset by 2026-07-08, we can run benchmarks and iterate.
[02:55] Ari: good. next section quick perf overview — we ran an internal dedicated test this week and saw 95th percentile ~210ms and p99 ~1.1s on our baseline config for avg 380-token prompts, baseline unquantized.
[03:12] Mark: 1.1s p99 is a touch high for customer SLAs, can you break down the cost numbers?
[03:21] Jess: rough numbers: on A100-style instances with batching off, cost per 1k tokens about $0.45 in the Dedicated config. using int8 quantization brings cost down ~30% but increases some variance in failure modes; we'll show quality comparisons.
[03:38] Liam: how bad is the quality delta? we can't accept hallucinations.
[03:44] Jess: for our curated evals, int8 gave a 0.5-1.2% drop in pass rate on constrained tasks; for open-ended generation the signal is noisier. recommendation: run quant evals on your prompts before toggling in prod.
[03:59] Mark: ok, please include a small eval harness when you share the perf plan.
[04:07] Jess: will do.
[04:10] Priya: back to security — audit logs retention is important for us, we need 12 months and export to our SIEM.
[04:20] Marcus (CSM): Redwood supports audit log export to S3 and we can configure retention; we'll share the exact retention configuration options.
[04:29] Priya: also SSO & RBAC, we need SAML/SCIM and fine-grained roles.
[04:36] Ari: we support SAML and SCIM, and role templates for admin/dev/readonly; Jess will attach the RBAC doc.
[04:45] Elena: any blockers on data residency? we need EU-only processing for a subset of users.
[04:52] Jess: we can route requests to EU-only regions and pin model variants there; make sure SaaS plan covers the EU region.
[05:01] Mark: great. can we talk about the perf test plan briefly?
[05:05] Jess: plan is: (1) small dry-run with anonymized prompts to validate connectivity, (2) run full perf suite with traffic shape that matches your production distributions, collect latency, cost, and token counts, (3) run quantization & batching variations, (4) produce a results report. we expect step 2 to take 1-2 days of steady runs.
[05:28] Mark: sounds good. what instance types will you use for the live run?
[05:31] Jess: we'll propose N1-style A100 and an M2-type for comparison; also a lower-cost 8-bit config to measure cost delta. we'll include exact SKUs in the perf plan.
[05:43] Samir: one more infra note — we'll need the hostname and certificate fingerprint before allowing peering, our security team scans certs.
[05:51] Ari: we'll provide cert details and the service CIDR.
[05:56] Elena: ok wrapping up, any open risks?
[06:00] Priya: main risk is access delays (VPC, KMS) and quantization quality gap.
[06:07] Ari: we'll mitigate by sending docs today and offering a fallback private-link for faster setup.
[06:12] Marcus: and we'll run a pre-test connectivity check to avoid wasted bench time.
[06:18] Mark: perfect. thanks everyone.
[06:21] Ari: recap of next steps: Ari share SOC2 pack and RBAC doc; Priya send VPC diagram; Jess send perf runbook; Mark provide sample prompts. we'll reconvene after the connectivity dry-run to kick off the live test.
[06:37] Elena: thanks all.
[06:40] [call ends]
notes: Transcription has occasional mis-hears (KV cash instead of KV cache, N1/M2 shorthand), speaker labels mostly correct. Links referenced: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack (SOC2/ISO summary), https://redwood.example.com/perf-playbook (perf runbook draft).
